summary:
Project Summary – BK SUPERNOVA | The Last Signal
The Last Signal: A Space Legacy Across Time is an interactive digital story we developed to introduce younger generations to the scientific legacy of NASA's space exploration missions and the equipment left behind in space. In our project, we created a seven-chapter journey through the past, present, and future, told from the perspective of a young student named Deniz. Using real NASA mission data, we incorporated the Apollo missions, scientific instruments left on the Moon, Mars rovers, the MOXIE experiment, and the Voyager probes. We also developed a fictional future scenario set in 2085, inspired by scientific knowledge. We enhanced our digital story with original illustrations, audio narration, interactive questions, and NASA resources, allowing students to explore and learn about space science in an engaging way. Our project addresses the challenge by highlighting the scientific legacy of spacecraft that have completed their missions or are still operating. Even when a spacecraft stops transmitting signals, the data it collected can continue to inspire new discoveries. Our message: A mission may end, but discovery never stops!
details:
Team: BK SUPERNOVA

1. Project Overview and Purpose

The Last Signal: A Journey Through NASA's Space Legacy is an interactive digital storytelling project designed to introduce students to the scientific achievements and lasting contributions of NASA's space missions. Our project focuses on an important question: What happens to the scientific legacy of spacecraft after their missions end? We aim to demonstrate that even when spacecraft stop functioning or transmitting signals, their discoveries, scientific measurements, and collected data continue to contribute to humanity's understanding of the universe.

2. How Does Our Project Work?

We developed a seven-chapter interactive digital story narrated from the perspective of a young student named Deniz. The story begins in the present, travels back to historical NASA missions, returns to current space exploration, and finally imagines a scientifically inspired future in 2085.Throughout the journey, users explore:

  • The Apollo missions and scientific equipment left on the Moon.
  • The Voyager 1 and Voyager 2 spacecraft and their journeys into interstellar space.
  • The Spirit and Opportunity Mars rovers and their scientific discoveries.
  • Curiosity, Perseverance, and the MOXIE oxygen-production experiment.
  • A fictional future in which scientists revisit the scientific legacy of earlier space missions.

Each chapter combines storytelling, space illustrations, scientific explanations, and interactive questions. Users can navigate between chapters, listen to English audio narration, explore NASA-related scientific information, and test their knowledge.

3. Technologies and Tools Used

Our project was developed as a browser-based digital experience using:

  • HTML: To structure the digital story and organize its chapters.
  • CSS: To design the visual interface, layouts, and responsive presentation.
  • JavaScript: To implement interactive navigation, quizzes, answer feedback, and audio controls.
  • Web Speech API: To provide English text-to-speech narration through compatible browsers.
  • Digital illustrations: To create an engaging visual experience for younger audiences.
  • NASA scientific resources: To support the historical missions and scientific information presented in the story.

The project can be opened in a compatible web browser without requiring specialized hardware.

4. Creativity and Innovation

What makes our project unique is the combination of scientific accuracy, creative storytelling, and interactive learning.

Instead of presenting NASA missions as separate facts or a traditional slideshow, we connect them through one continuous narrative.

Our story moves between the past, present, and future, helping students understand how earlier scientific discoveries influence current research and inspire future exploration.

The fictional 2085 chapter encourages students to imagine how today's scientific knowledge could be used by future generations. We clearly distinguish this imagined scenario from documented NASA missions.

5. Benefits and Educational Impact

Our project aims to make space science more accessible, engaging, and understandable for school-aged students.

Through interactive storytelling, students can develop scientific curiosity, critical thinking, digital literacy, and an appreciation for the importance of scientific research.

We also hope to encourage students to recognize that scientific progress is a continuous process built upon the achievements of previous generations.

The digital format allows the story to be used in classrooms, science clubs, and independent learning activities.

6. Design Considerations

While developing our project, we considered scientific reliability, age-appropriate language, accessibility, visual engagement, and ease of use.

We used NASA mission information as the scientific foundation of the story and identified fictional future events separately to avoid confusing imagination with established scientific facts.

We also incorporated interactive questions and audio narration to support different learning preferences.

7. Our Vision

Our goal is to inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, and space explorers by demonstrating that every mission leaves behind knowledge that can shape the future.

A spacecraft may send its last signal, but its scientific legacy continues to speak to future generations.

Our message: A mission may end, but discovery never stops!
